subject: Multinomial Logit Model, problem with dimensions

messages.author: 47847628200bd730
messages.subject: Multinomial Logit Model, problem with dimensions
parts:
Good afternoon! 
I`m new Stan user. My question can be silly but I really need your help.

I`m writing a choice model with the following data in R: each individual offered С cards. Each card has K alternatives. So, each person need to choose 1 of the K alternatives on each card. 

model_bayesian_multi_logit <- "
data {
    int N; // number of people 
    int<lower=2> K; // number of alternatives on each card
    int<lower=1> D; // number of attributes that characterizes alternatives 
    int<lower=1> C; // number of cards
    matrix[K, D] X[N, C]; // matriсes for different people and cards with all characteristics 
    int y[N, C]; // each individual choices for each card 
parameters {
    vector[D] beta;
}
model {
    for (d in 1:D)
        beta[d] ~ normal(0, 5);
    for (n in 1:N)
        for (c in 1:C)
        y[n, c] ~ categorical_logit(X[n, c]*beta);
}
"

Then I`m trying to check the model with the simplest example:
N <- 1
C <- 1
D <- 3
K <- 2
y <- 1
dim(y) <- c(1, 1)

X <- array(data = c(1, 1, 1.5, 1.5, 170, 250, 120, 150), dim = c(2, 3, 1, 1))
Where X looks like that (intuitively this is correct for the given N, C, D, K, because we got an array for only 1 person and 1 card, hence, 1 matrix in total) 
     [,1] [,2] [,3]
[1,]    1  1.5  170
[2,]    1  1.5  250
Individual is supposed to choose between 2 rows which characterizes 2 different alternatives.

random_data <- list(N = N, y = y, X = X, D = D, C = C, K = K)
fit_logit <- stan(model_code = model_bayesian_multi_logit, data = random_data, iter = 1000, chains = 4)

Stan tells me I`m wrong with X dimension:

Error in eval(substitute(expr), envir, enclos) : 
  mismatch in dimension declared and found in context; processing stage=data initialization; variable name=X; position=0; dims declared=(1,1,2,3); dims found=(2,3,1,1)
failed to create the sampler; sampling not done

I can rewrite X like that:
X <- array(data = c(1, 1, 1.5, 1.5, 170, 250, 120, 150), dim = c(1,1,2,3))
Where X looks like that (this is weird, since i need to have 1 matrix for 1 person and 1 card)  

, , 1, 1

     [,1]
[1,]    1

, , 2, 1

     [,1]
[1,]    1

, , 1, 2

     [,1]
[1,]  1.5

, , 2, 2

     [,1]
[1,]  1.5

, , 1, 3

     [,1]
[1,]  170

, , 2, 3

     [,1]
[1,]  250

In this case Stan will work and give me the results but I think this is a wrong way (for the given example the answer looks right but for 1 person with 2 cards or more complicated cases it is wrong).

Well, I guess R and Stan have different perceptions of the dimension. Moreover, it seems that Stan stores arrays in a row-major order, while R in a column-major order. 
The question is the following: how do I need to transform X to be sure that Stan understands me correctly?

Hope, I described the problem clearly. Thank you in advance!

messages.author: 61924cbc2e733aae
messages.subject: Re: Multinomial Logit Model, problem with dimensions
parts:
Hi,

What you have in Stan is an array (N, C) dimensions whose elements are matrices of (K, D)  dimensions.
In R you need to shape the array in a way that you end with four dimensions (N, C, K, D) that you can supply to Stan. Even if arrays in R are column-major, and in Stan are in row-major, the program does the pertinent transformations.

You could use the print statement to check if the elements of the array that you pass ends in the right positions.
